### Structure, pacing, and consequence

Anthem gains much of its effect from sequence. Setup creates expectations; complications test those expectations; revelations or emotional turns force revision. Pacing therefore has an interpretive function. A fast passage can reduce reflection and increase uncertainty, while a slower passage can make motive, atmosphere, setting, social order, or relationship dynamics more visible. ### Character and responsibility

The most useful character question is not whether someone is simply good, bad, right, or wrong. It is what the character wants, what the character believes, which information is missing, and what cost follows from acting on that belief. This keeps Anthem from being flattened into a moral diagram. It also makes room for contradiction: people can be perceptive in one area and self-deceiving in another, loyal yet controlling, frightened yet reckless, sincere while still causing harm, or confident while misunderstanding the situation.

Any summary removes texture.
